reason: The cited evidence (E1) shows that increasing Al2O3 content reduces wear and friction, but it does not address in situ formation of α-Al2O3 from Al addition to CoCrFeNi. E2 explicitly states that aluminum oxide grows slowly and forms only discontinuous Al2O3 nanoparticles, not a continuous tribolayer, and that a protective glaze layer relies on Nb/V-rich oxides, not Al2O3. Thus, the key premises of a continuous, self-adaptive α-Al2O3 tribolayer and its efficacy across the full temperature range are contradicted or unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Adding Al to CoCrFeNi will form a continuous α-Al2O3 tribolayer during sliding from RT to 800 °C
The α-Al2O3 tribolayer will reduce friction and wear across the full temperature range
Al addition promotes preferential oxidation and a self-replenishing lubricious film
At lower temperatures, a nascent lubricious oxide can form with optimization or catalytic additions
